items.content: Before the birds remembered their purpose and the street lamps had grown weary of their vigil, she rose into a darkness that felt personally hers. The house breathed around her in its slow nocturnal rhythm, each creak and settling groan familiar yet strange, like words in a language almost forgotten. She stood at the window and watched the sky hold its deep blue secret, the world suspended in that rare, unclaimed hour belonging to no one — or perhaps, she thought, to anyone willing to wake for it.

items.content: The world below arranges itself into something almost mathematical from this height — the harbor's crooked arm, the white ribbons of road threading through salt-bleached dunes, the sailboats reduced to small bright punctuation on an otherwise indifferent sea. The air up here carries a different quality, thinner and sharper, smelling of iron and distance. You rest your hands on the railing and feel, for a suspended moment, that you are standing at the very edge of what can be known.

items.content: You don't know about me without you have read a book by the name of The Adventures of Tom Sawyer; but that ain't no matter.

items.content: The light falls through tall windows in long, unhurried slabs, settling across the spines of books like something between dust and gold. A woman turns a page near the periodicals, and the sound carries farther than it should. Time moves differently here — not slowly exactly, but with a kind of deliberateness, as though the hours have remembered their manners. Even the air seems to hold itself still, respectful of all the unfinished thoughts pressed between these covers.
